name: בֵּל
summary: The chief god of Babylon, whose title Bēl “lord” is Akkadian bēlu, the same word as Hebrew בַּעַל. Isaiah sees him bowing down and carried off as a burden on beasts, unable to save, while Yahweh carries his people from the womb to old age (Isa 46:1–4); Jeremiah sets him beside Merodach (Marduk) as shamed when Babylon is taken (Jer 50:2), and Yahweh will punish Bel in Babylon and make him disgorge what he swallowed (Jer 51:44).

evidence.note: “Bel bows down, Nebo stoops; their idols are on the beasts.”
“You who have been borne by me from the womb … I will carry and will deliver.”
“Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed”: Bel parallel to Marduk.
“I will punish Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed.”

note: A loan from Akkadian, not a Hebrew form of בַּעַל; filed under בעל because the word is the same Semitic word and BDB files it here. TIPNR's Supernatural record Bel@Isa.46.1.
